tools.name: ask_lead
tools.description: Ask the thread lead a question and wait for the answer.

input_schema.description: Ask the thread lead a question and wait for the answer.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a question (a card on the web page). Either a plain question (question + optional options) or up to 4 structured questions (questions: each with a short header, 2-4 options with a description, one may be recommended, multi_select for several answers; the user can always type their own answer instead). Members block until the user answers and get the answer back; the coordinator and leads get the question id at once and receive "[Answer to q5] ..." as a later message. Give question or questions.

input_schema.description: Ask the user a question (a card on the web page). Either a plain question (question + optional options) or up to 4 structured questions (questions: each with a short header, 2-4 options with a description, one may be recommended, multi_select for several answers; the user can always type their own answer instead). Members block until the user answers and get the answer back; the coordinator and leads get the question id at once and receive "[Answer to q5] ..." as a later message. Give question or questions.

question.description: A plain question (use questions for choices with descriptions).

options.description: Suggested answers shown as buttons (with question).

questions.description: Structured questions shown as one card, like Claude Code's AskUserQuestion.

question.description: The complete question, ending with a question mark.

header.description: Very short label shown as a chip (max 12 characters).

options.description: 2-4 distinct choices; an "other" free-text answer is always offered, do not add one.

recommended.description: Mark the option you recommend (at most one per question).

multi_select.description: Let the user pick several options.

via.description: Set by the platform when Claude's built-in AskUserQuestion is routed here (the call then blocks for every tier). Do not set it yourself.

tools.name: assign_subtask
tools.description: Create a subtask of your current task for a teammate (instance or role name); returns the task id at once. Only for roles with can_delegate.

input_schema.description: Create a subtask of your current task for a teammate (instance or role name); returns the task id at once. Only for roles with can_delegate.

tools.name: assign_task
tools.description: Create a task under a main task. assignee is an instance name (dev-2) to assign directly, or a role name (dev) to put it in the task pool where the first free instance claims it.

input_schema.description: Create a task under a main task. assignee is an instance name (dev-2) to assign directly, or a role name (dev) to put it in the task pool where the first free instance claims it.

main.description: Title of the main task (plan step) this belongs to.

repo.description: Repository the task is about (owner/name); named in the task text. With base, records the thread's base branch in it.

base.description: Base branch the thread uses in repo (only before the thread branch exists there; read the project context for stated bases).

tools.name: broadcast
tools.description: Send a message to every member of the thread.

input_schema.description: Send a message to every member of the thread.

tools.name: cancel_task
tools.description: Cancel a task that has not finished.

input_schema.description: Cancel a task that has not finished.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Finish your current task explicitly; the platform pushes your branch first. Use status failed when you cannot finish it.

input_schema.description: Finish your current task explicitly; the platform pushes your branch first. Use status failed when you cannot finish it.

artifacts.description: Paths, commit SHAs or URLs produced by the task.

tools.name: enqueue_merge
tools.description: Put a member branch into the merge queue, one entry per repository the task pushed (merged into the thread branch on GitHub, then CI). Give either member or task_id.

input_schema.description: Put a member branch into the merge queue, one entry per repository the task pushed (merged into the thread branch on GitHub, then CI). Give either member or task_id.

repo.description: Merge only this repository of the task (default: every repository the task pushed).

base.description: Base branch the thread uses in repo (only before the thread branch exists there; read the project context for stated bases).

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Write the thread summary; it is also added to the project memory. With code changes, call it after open_pr: the thread ends when the PR merges. A thread that changed no repository (research, review, Q&A) needs no PR: finish ends it right away (done).

input_schema.description: Write the thread summary; it is also added to the project memory. With code changes, call it after open_pr: the thread ends when the PR merges. A thread that changed no repository (research, review, Q&A) needs no PR: finish ends it right away (done).

tools.name: forward_to_thread
tools.description: Forward the user's own project-chat messages, word for word with their images, files and @ references, to a thread's lead (thread_no; a finished thread is reopened, an archived one refuses) or into a new thread (new_thread, the messages become its brief). The lead receives them as the user's words; use this instead of paraphrasing when the request belongs to a thread. Each user message ends with [message_id: N]; without message_ids the user's latest messages are forwarded.

input_schema.description: Forward the user's own project-chat messages, word for word with their images, files and @ references, to a thread's lead (thread_no; a finished thread is reopened, an archived one refuses) or into a new thread (new_thread, the messages become its brief). The lead receives them as the user's words; use this instead of paraphrasing when the request belongs to a thread. Each user message ends with [message_id: N]; without message_ids the user's latest messages are forwarded.

new_thread.description: Open a new thread for the messages instead of thread_no.

message_ids.description: The user's messages to forward ([message_id: N] at the end of each), any order.

latest.description: Without message_ids: forward the user's latest N messages (default 1).

note.description: Optional short note of yours sent along (context the lead needs; never a rewrite of the user's words).

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Show a task: instruction, status, dependencies and result.

input_schema.description: Show a task: instruction, status, dependencies and result.

tools.name: list_deliverables
tools.description: List this project's deliverables (designs, documents… from every thread), newest first: id, title, kind, versions, who published the latest version, thread and when it changed. Use read_deliverable to fetch one's files.

input_schema.description: List this project's deliverables (designs, documents… from every thread), newest first: id, title, kind, versions, who published the latest version, thread and when it changed. Use read_deliverable to fetch one's files.

thread.description: Only deliverables of this thread number.

kind.description: Only this kind (design, doc, slides, dashboard, board, data).

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List the thread's tasks with assignee, main task, kind and status.

input_schema.description: List the thread's tasks with assignee, main task, kind and status.

tools.name: list_team
tools.description: List the thread team: name, role, type, node and current task of each member.

input_schema.description: List the thread team: name, role, type, node and current task of each member.

tools.name: list_threads
tools.description: List threads, one line each: number, title, status, main-task progress and how many items wait for the user.

input_schema.description: List threads, one line each: number, title, status, main-task progress and how many items wait for the user.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a project memory topic file and its line in MEMORY.md (MEMORY.md itself cannot be deleted).

input_schema.description: Delete a project memory topic file and its line in MEMORY.md (MEMORY.md itself cannot be deleted).

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List the project's memory files (MEMORY.md and topic files) with their descriptions.

input_schema.description: List the project's memory files (MEMORY.md and topic files) with their descriptions.

tools.name: memory_read
tools.description: Read one project memory file in full (MEMORY.md or a topic file listed in it).

input_schema.description: Read one project memory file in full (MEMORY.md or a topic file listed in it).

tools.name: memory_write
tools.description: Create or replace a project memory file. A topic file (e.g. testing.md) needs a one-line description; the platform keeps its line in MEMORY.md. name MEMORY.md rewrites the index itself.

input_schema.description: Create or replace a project memory file. A topic file (e.g. testing.md) needs a one-line description; the platform keeps its line in MEMORY.md. name MEMORY.md rewrites the index itself.

tools.name: message_thread
tools.description: Send a message to a thread's lead as the project coordinator.

input_schema.description: Send a message to a thread's lead as the project coordinator.

tools.name: open_pr
tools.description: Open one pull request per repository the thread changed (thread branch to that repository's base branch); the thread moves to review. Only for code changes: a thread that changed nothing ends with finish alone.

input_schema.description: Open one pull request per repository the thread changed (thread branch to that repository's base branch); the thread moves to review. Only for code changes: a thread that changed nothing ends with finish alone.

repo.description: Open only this repository's pull request (default: every changed repository without one).

base.description: PR base branch for repo (or for the only repository to open); default the thread's base there.

tools.name: open_thread
tools.description: Open a new thread (number, branch, member instances) for a piece of work; the brief becomes the lead's first message. Returns #no immediately.

input_schema.description: Open a new thread (number, branch, member instances) for a piece of work; the brief becomes the lead's first message. Returns #no immediately.

roles.description: Role names to staff the thread with; default = all member roles of the team.

repos.description: Repositories of the project the thread should work in, with an optional explicit base branch each (when the project context states one).

base.description: Base branch for this repository; default its default branch.

message_id.description: The user's message (its [message_id: N]) this thread is opened for; it is shown with the brief and its images and files go to the lead. Default: the user's latest message in the project chat.

tools.name: publish_deliverable
tools.description: Register a deliverable link for the project (doc, design, slides, dashboard, board, data...). Pull requests are not deliverables (the platform tracks them on the thread).

input_schema.description: Register a deliverable link for the project (doc, design, slides, dashboard, board, data...). Pull requests are not deliverables (the platform tracks them on the thread).

kind.description: Known: doc, design, slides, dashboard, board, data; anything else is shown as a link. Not pr: pull requests are tracked by the platform on the thread and are not deliverables.

tools.name: publish_file
tools.description: Publish a file you made (HTML prototype, Markdown doc, SVG, image, PDF, JSON, CSV) as a project deliverable. The platform uploads it from your working directory and hosts it; people view it on the Deliverables page and their comments come back to you as messages. A directory with index.html is published as a small site. Pass deliverable_id to publish a new version of an earlier deliverable.

input_schema.description: Publish a file you made (HTML prototype, Markdown doc, SVG, image, PDF, JSON, CSV) as a project deliverable. The platform uploads it from your working directory and hosts it; people view it on the Deliverables page and their comments come back to you as messages. A directory with index.html is published as a small site. Pass deliverable_id to publish a new version of an earlier deliverable.

path.description: File (or directory with index.html) inside your working directory, relative to it.

kind.description: design for prototypes and visual designs, doc for documents and specs; also slides, dashboard, board, data.

deliverable_id.description: An earlier deliverable of this project published with publish_file; the file becomes its next version.

tools.name: push_branch
tools.description: Push the HEAD of each of your repository checkouts that has new commits to your member branch (thread/<no>/<name>). You have no write token yourself; commit first, then call this.

input_schema.description: Push the HEAD of each of your repository checkouts that has new commits to your member branch (thread/<no>/<name>). You have no write token yourself; commit first, then call this.

tools.name: read_deliverable
tools.description: Fetch the files of a deliverable published with publish_file (any thread of this project) into your working directory under .agent-deliverables/<id>/v<version>/ (git-ignored; a multi-file site keeps its folders). Returns the local folder, the file list, the version history and the user's comments. To revise it: edit the files there, then publish_file(path=<that folder or file>, deliverable_id=<id>) to publish the next version.

input_schema.description: Fetch the files of a deliverable published with publish_file (any thread of this project) into your working directory under .agent-deliverables/<id>/v<version>/ (git-ignored; a multi-file site keeps its folders). Returns the local folder, the file list, the version history and the user's comments. To revise it: edit the files there, then publish_file(path=<that folder or file>, deliverable_id=<id>) to publish the next version.

version.description: Version to fetch; the latest when omitted.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Return your unread messages (including broadcasts) and mark them read.

input_schema.description: Return your unread messages (including broadcasts) and mark them read.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Append a one-line note to the project memory index MEMORY.md (shortcut for small facts).

input_schema.description: Append a one-line note to the project memory index MEMORY.md (shortcut for small facts).

tools.name: reply_to
tools.description: Answer a member's question ("[Question q3 from dev-1 ...]"). Answer quickly: the member is blocked until you do.

input_schema.description: Answer a member's question ("[Question q3 from dev-1 ...]"). Answer quickly: the member is blocked until you do.

tools.name: report_progress
tools.description: Report progress on your task (shown in the thread activity).

input_schema.description: Report progress on your task (shown in the thread activity).

tools.name: request_review
tools.description: Ask a teammate to review your work (creates a review task under your current task) and wait for the result. You cannot ask yourself.

input_schema.description: Ask a teammate to review your work (creates a review task under your current task) and wait for the result. You cannot ask yourself.

tools.name: review_permission
tools.description: Decide a member's permission request ("[Permission request q5 from dev-1 ...]"). allow lets the member run it once, deny refuses it (the reason goes to the member), ask_user hands it to the user. Choose ask_user when unsure, or when it touches secrets, production, money, other people or anything irreversible. Decide quickly: the member waits.

input_schema.description: Decide a member's permission request ("[Permission request q5 from dev-1 ...]"). allow lets the member run it once, deny refuses it (the reason goes to the member), ask_user hands it to the user. Choose ask_user when unsure, or when it touches secrets, production, money, other people or anything irreversible. Decide quickly: the member waits.

reason.description: One sentence; shown to the user in the thread's activity and on the card.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Leave a message for a teammate (instance name) or for the lead ("lead"). Busy recipients get it after their current turn.

input_schema.description: Leave a message for a teammate (instance name) or for the lead ("lead"). Busy recipients get it after their current turn.

tools.name: set_status
tools.description: Set your speech-bubble text in the office (one short sentence on what you are doing). Call it when you switch work; it does not change your state or position and expires after 10 minutes.

input_schema.description: Set your speech-bubble text in the office (one short sentence on what you are doing). Call it when you switch work; it does not change your state or position and expires after 10 minutes.

tools.name: tell_user
tools.description: Post a short message to the user in the thread conversation right away (shown as the lead's own message), without ending the turn. Use it for the receipt after the brief and for updates the user should see; it is not a question (use ask_user to ask).

input_schema.description: Post a short message to the user in the thread conversation right away (shown as the lead's own message), without ending the turn. Use it for the receipt after the brief and for updates the user should see; it is not a question (use ask_user to ask).

tools.name: thread_status
tools.description: Show one thread: plan, recent activity, the lead's latest reply and the PR.

input_schema.description: Show one thread: plan, recent activity, the lead's latest reply and the PR.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Replace the thread plan (main tasks). Steps are matched by title so existing main tasks keep their ids.

input_schema.description: Replace the thread plan (main tasks). Steps are matched by title so existing main tasks keep their ids.

tools.name: wait_task
tools.description: Wait until one of your subtasks finishes and return its result. Only for roles with can_delegate.

input_schema.description: Wait until one of your subtasks finishes and return its result. Only for roles with can_delegate.
